prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: illustrated mobile hotpot tile-puzzle game background, tall portrait 720:1520.
Primary request: Create 徽州水墨, a richly painted Huizhou ink-and-porcelain tavern alcove game background, using the two supplied images solely as composition and craftsmanship references. It must look like a new fully illustrated environment rather than just a color filter.
Composition invariants: exact tall portrait aspect of references. Upper decorative header occupies y=0–14%. A huge EMPTY pale warm ivory rice-paper playing area fills x=10–90%, y=16–73.5%; no illustrations, landscapes, objects, text or patterns with high contrast in its middle. Decor only at far edges. Straight wooden tabletop horizon at y=73.5%; table occupies remaining bottom. Copper hotpot with red broth partially cropped bottom-left. Porcelain chopstick holder, chopsticks and very small props clustered bottom-right. No tray, food tiles, buttons, people or phone frame.
Scene: at top, a dark ink-grey Huizhou roof eave and exquisitely carved black wood lintel, with pale oyster-grey silk drape beneath, restrained muted gold joining details. At sides whitewashed plaster pillars, fine dark carved lattice, two small warm cream hanging lanterns with no writing. A blank creamy rice-paper hanging scroll seamlessly forms the vast central space. Extremely faint ink mountain hints are restricted to far edges. A bonsai pine and blue-and-white porcelain vase at lower left edge and graceful plum twig in porcelain at lower right edge. Dark weathered oak tabletop and warm copper hotpot. Refined black, oyster white and grey identity with only restrained muted gold and cobalt porcelain accents.
Style/medium: richly detailed painterly casual mobile game illustration like references, tactile wood grain, weathered plaster, rice paper fiber, handpainted blue-white porcelain, warm luminous shadows, immersive finely rendered materials. Calm sophisticated Huizhou aesthetics. Not monochrome flat sketch, not vector, not photoreal.
Text: none whatsoever.
Avoid: letters, calligraphy, Chinese characters, numbers, logos, watermarks, UI, buttons, trays, food tile cards, menus, phone frame, people. Keep center EMPTY, keep tabletop height and side prop scale consistent with references.
